content.text: Section 20 meets the preferred position, and indemnity obligations are carved out of the cap as "Excluded Claims." No redline needed.

input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 satisfies the preferred position in full. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables (20.1), and separately for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2) — matching limbs (a)-(d) of our model language. Standard procedure is present and balanced (20.4: prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-limited notice failure, and consent required for settlements admitting fault or not fully releasing the indemnified Party). The infringement remedy ladder in 20.5 (procure, modify/replace without materially reducing functionality, else terminate and refund on a straight-line three-year basis, with no right to terminate unaffected Services) exceeds the fallback. Notably, Vendor's IP indemnity in 20.1 carries none of the usual Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions, which is more favourable to us than either position. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 stays narrow as required — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with express carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or Vendor instructions. On the cap interaction, indemnification obligations are "Excluded Claims" under 21.3 and therefore fall outside the Section 21.1 liability cap entirely, which is better than the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap. (The narrow cap base in 21.1 — Fees under the first Order Form only — is a limitation-of-liability issue addressed under that rule and does not affect this indemnity, which is uncapped.) No redline warranted.
